1.say: Solve seven to the power X minus one equals five to the power X minus three, to three significant figures.
asks: What does to the power X minus one mean?

5.say: Now bring the powers down, with the law Bring down power: log of A to the N is N times log A.
asks: Why does the power come down?

do.text: Bring down power: $\lg a^n = n\lg a$

6.say: X minus one comes down in front of log seven.
asks: Why can the power come down?

7.say: And X minus three comes down in front of log five.

11.say: Divide both sides by log seven minus log five, to get X on its own.
asks: Why divide by log 7 minus log 5?

13.say: Watch out: do not write X is about eight point five seven. Rounding never removes the minus.

do.text: ✗ Watch out: keep the minus, not $x \approx 8.57$
